author: Eve Qiao
description:
Australia has returned two stone sculptures to China after more than 30 years abroad.
The statues, showing the heads of a military official and civil servant, had been given to the National Gallery of Australia in Canberra by a private collector and date back to the Northern Song dynasty (960–1127).
China’s National Cultural Heritage Administration received the heads on Wednesday, according to the state broadcaster CCTV.
They are thought to have been removed from two imperial mausoleums in Henan...
title: Australia returns ancient stone heads to China after more than 30 years

author: Eleni Stefania Kalapoda
description:
On a hillside in Anji, in Zhejiang province, a cluster of umbrella-like canopies steps gently down the slope, following the rows of tea bushes. There is no grand entrance, no plinth, no monumental block of stone. On October 22, at Dutch Design Week in Eindhoven, this project, Anji Hood by RoarcRenew Architects, was named Cultural Space of the Year at the Frame Awards 2026, chosen from more than 1,000 submissions by 100 jurors across 10 panels.
I served on the Frame Awards 2026 grand jury for the...
title: What China’s best new cultural spaces have in common: the light touch

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced additional military cooperation funding for the Philippines and agreed with Manila on efforts for enhanced interoperability between their forces on Wednesday, as Washington sought to strengthen its defence posture along the first island chain.
The Pentagon disclosed neither the size of the funding increase nor a timetable for the coordination initiative following Hegseth’s meeting with Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jnr in Cebu on the...
title: Hegseth pledges stronger military framework with Philippines, but lacks details

author: Mark Magnier
description:
Huawei Technologies started presenting its case on Wednesday, arguing that as a cutting-edge global tech leader it had no interest in stealing trade secrets, in a high-stakes criminal trial involving dozens of witnesses, legions of lawyers and untold millions of US dollars in legal fees.
The Shenzhen-based company has pleaded not guilty to 14 criminal counts in New York’s Eastern District Court, including racketeering conspiracy, bank fraud, wire fraud and trade secret theft spanning more than...
title: Huawei opens defence in US criminal trial, touting its record of innovation

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Real Madrid has issued an apology to China over Kylian Mbappe’s controversial remarks about the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, after the Spanish football club’s initial response failed to quell anger in China.
In a statement published on its website on Wednesday, the club apologised to the Chinese people for “any discomfort” caused by the French footballer’s remarks, a day after Mbappe issued his own public apology.
The apology came after Chinese state broadcaster CCTV Sports rejected Real...
title: Real Madrid issues apology to China over Mbappe’s Mao remarks

author: Ling Xin
description:
When a star like our sun grows old, it puffs up into a red giant that can gobble up its nearest planets.
But Chinese astronomers say they have found three solar systems where planets should have been eaten this way yet somehow survived – a puzzle that could change how scientists picture Earth’s distant future.
Using Nasa’s TESS space telescope, a team led by Qian Shengbang from Yunnan University showed that three Jupiter-like planets – each hugging an ageing star in the northern sky – had lived...
title: Chinese astronomers find planets that somehow avoided death by red giant stars

author: Shi Huang
description:
Four seriously ill Chinese boys who would almost certainly have died in their twenties from a rare inherited disease received the same highly anticipated gene-editing drug.
More than a year later, a set of cruel and contradictory data emerged.
Two boys gained the strength to walk farther. One boy showed no improvement in gait and subsequently withdrew from the trial. And the fourth boy’s heart stopped beating 81 hours after receiving the medication intravenously, owing to a severe systemic...
title: In China gene-editing trial, 2 children improved, 1 died and 1 withdrew

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s trip to the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday echoed the intense coordination that preceded his previous summits with US President Donald Trump.
Between March 2018 and June 2019, Kim met Chinese President Xi Jinping five times across Beijing, Dalian and Pyongyang, and three of those occasions happened not long before his summits with Trump.
Yet, while Saturday’s unannounced visit appeared superficially similar, analysts said the strategic focus had...
title: Why Kim Jong-un’s border trip to China differs from past pre-summit playbooks

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
A rare satellite image of China’s secretive spaceplane has appeared in a new US intelligence report that warned Beijing was expanding its ability to track American forces and could deploy space-based directed-energy weapons by the late 2020s.
The US Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA) report published on Sunday included an image of the reusable spacecraft, credited to satellite imagery firm Maxar in 2024, showing its shuttle-like design and apparent solar arrays.
A spaceplane is a spacecraft...
title: US warns China is expanding its space toolkit with spaceplane and energy weapons

author: Amber Wang
description:
The People’s Liberation Army (PLA) has held defence strategy consultations with France and Germany over the past week despite mounting trade tensions between Beijing and Europe.
A PLA strategy consultation delegation visited France and Germany from October 21 to 28 for the talks, according to a statement released by China’s defence ministry on Wednesday.
The Chinese delegation engaged in in-depth exchanges of views with the two countries separately on bilateral and military-to-military...
title: China’s military holds talks in France and Germany despite rising trade tensions

author: Amber Wang
description:
Former Chinese vice-premier Liu Yandong died of illness on Wednesday at the age of 80. She was one of China’s most prominent female leaders, playing a pivotal role in the country’s united front work and education sector.
The official obituary released by Xinhua described Liu as an “outstanding leader in the [Communist] Party’s united front work, in China’s education, science and technology, healthcare, and women and children’s affairs.”
Liu was vice-premier from 2013 to 2018. She was the fourth...
title: China’s former vice-premier Liu Yandong dies at age 80

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
China said it would seek India’s help to “maintain peace and stability in the border areas” after new stand-offs in a long-disputed region threatened to undermine improved relations.
“We hope that India will work with China in the same direction by jointly implementing the common understandings between the two sides,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a daily media briefing on Monday. China “strictly abides by the relevant agreements”, he said.
Guo also said that China...
title: China seeks India’s help in defusing border tensions

author: Fan Chen
description:
Massive crowds, fireworks and dancing have filled the streets across Belgrade since Serbia’s nationalist strongman Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in Sunday’s parliamentary election after 14 years in power.
The political shift could cool diplomatic ties between Beijing and Belgrade and invite sharper scrutiny of Chinese investments in Serbia, but was unlikely to upend a relationship built on years of cooperation, analysts argued.
Vucic conceded the defeat of his right-wing Serbian Progressive...
title: Why China’s ties with Serbia face scrutiny, not severance, after historic Vucic loss

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
A Chinese investigative blogger who exposed telecoms fraud and other illegal activity was killed by criminals hired on social media, according to Chinese media, as the case prompts calls for heavier punishment for his death.
The body of Wu Kai, who used the name “Huijian” on social media and had written for years about telecoms fraud in Southeast Asia, was discovered in southern China in November 2024. His death and details of the case that followed have been revealed this week.
In August 2024,...
title: Chinese anti-scam blogger killed by contractors hired online to silence his work

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
After convincing China to accept a cap on its hybrid car exports, a stream of top-level European finance and banking officials will descend on the Chinese capital in the coming months on a far trickier mission: persuading Beijing to stop holding down its currency to help save the bloc’s struggling industry.
In the week of November 23, top European Union economy officials led by director general Maarten Verwey will sit down in Beijing for a “macroeconomic dialogue” with their Chinese...
title: EU plans high-level China currency talks as fears of new trade shock mount

author: SCMP
description:
ICBC share prices diverge after first parallel listing
By Carol Chan
This article was first published on October 28, 2006
Shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China jumped a relatively modest 14.7 per cent on their Hong Kong debut and a lacklustre 5.1 per cent in Shanghai as the world’s largest-ever initial public offering finally came to market.
The debut immediately catapulted China’s largest lender into the top ranks of global banks as measured by market capitalisation. It seized the...
title: ICBC makes history with record US$19 billion IPO in dual listing in 2006 - SCMP archive

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China’s massive maritime science infrastructure – an aircraft carrier-sized floating artificial island – has officially entered its engineering construction phase.
On October 18, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), the facility’s lead developer, signed a construction contract worth over 2.7 billion yuan (US$405 million) with a shipbuilder under China State Shipbuilding Corporation, according to local media reports.
The semi-submersible twin-hull platform is the world’s first mobile,...
title: China formally launches project to build aircraft carrier-sized ‘science island’

author: William Zheng
description:
Beijing has appointed veteran propaganda official Mo Gaoyi as Communist Party secretary of Yunnan province in its latest leadership reshuffle, making him a rare example this year of a provincial head with minimal local governance experience.
An analyst said that the move could reflect Beijing’s efforts to broaden the talent selection criteria for some senior roles, allowing specialists to take on important generalist positions.
Mo – director of the State Council Information Office (SCIO) and a...
title: Why has Beijing appointed a propaganda veteran to lead a border province?

author: Mengzhen Liu,Ziya Guo
description:
Manila sent two strikingly different messages to Beijing on October 13. At the Malacanang Palace, a presidential spokeswoman reaffirmed Manila’s commitment to sustaining diplomatic and economic ties with China, saying “China needs the Philippines, and the Philippines needs China”.
That same day, Philippine Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jnr rejected a call for military-to-military communication with China, a move that received public support from the Armed Forces of the Philippines. Teodoro...
title: Manila speaks with 2 voices on China

author: Nayan Seth
description:
An American student considering studying in China attended a briefing with a senior FBI official at a Washington think tank last month to address her concerns about whether such an experience could jeopardise her prospects for a career in the federal government.
The official’s message: travelling to China would not automatically disqualify her.
She welcomed the clarification but said she wasn’t “completely reassured”.
“I’m still wondering if it’s a good idea to go,” said the student, who...
title: Will China travel hurt US students’ careers? FBI battles fears as talent pipeline stalls

author: Chao Kong
description:
Lithium deposits formed by ancient volcanic activity may lie beneath parts of China’s battery manufacturing heartland, particularly along the southeastern coast, according to a new study.
In an interview with the South China Morning Post, geologist Duan Zheng said that “potential targets for clay-type lithium deposits in southeastern China overlap with lithium battery industrial clusters in East and South China”.
“Local supplies could significantly reduce transport costs and supply-chain risks,”...
title: China’s battery factories could be sitting right on top of vast lithium deposits
